readout_other: Immunofluorescence staining for amyloid plaques and Iba1/CD86 (M1) and Iba1/CD206 (M2) microglial markers; ELISA for Aβ42, IL-10, TNF-α; TMT-based quantitative proteomics; Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) activity assay
direction_notes: Study did not assess excitatory/inhibitory neural effects; ultrasound stimulation shifted microglial polarization from M1 to M2, reduced amyloid plaque load and Aβ42, and increased anti-inflammatory IL-10.

exposures.label: Hippocampal ultrasound stimulation in APP/PS1 mice

timing.protocol_description: The excitation voltage was set at 330 mVpp, and Ispta was calculated to be 294 mW/cm² based on measured sound pressure. The PRF was set to 40 Hz. The remaining parameters were set as follows: DC = 10%, SD = 5 s, ISI = 5 s. The ultrasonic probe was targeted at the hippocampus (1.8 mm posterior, 1 mm lateral to Bregma) for 30 min per day (15 min on the left and 15 min on the right side) for 5 days.

source_quotes.n_subjects: an AD model ultrasound stimulation treatment group (US group; APP/PS1, n = 11)
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Ultrasound stimulation was used to stimulate the hippocampus for 30 min per day for 5 days in the ultrasound stimulation‐treated group.
source_quotes.randomised: Mice were grouped according to random digits table generated by computer software.
source_quotes.sham_type: Mice in the sham treatment group were shaved and anesthetized in the same way as mice in the US group but ultrasound stimulation placed on the head was not turned on.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The attenuation coefficient of biological tissue is nearly proportional to the ultrasound frequency, so this study employed a frequency of 1 MHz, a parameter that has also been widely used in most brain ultrasound stimulation studies [21, 27].
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: To ensure the safety of the animals and stay within the energy output range of the ultrasound equipment, the excitation voltage was set at 330 mVpp, and Ispta was calculated to be 294 mW/cm² based on measured sound pressure.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: Since 40 Hz gamma oscillations have been shown to play a positive role in clearing Aβ plaques [28], the PRF was set to 40 Hz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: The remaining parameters were set as follows: DC = 10%, SD = 5 s, ISI = 5 s.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: The remaining parameters were set as follows: DC = 10%, SD = 5 s, ISI = 5 s.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: The device amplifies the waveform from a transducer (V303‐SU; Olympus) by a power amplifier (1040 L; E&I) to emit ultrasonic waves.
source_quotes.exposures[0].target.label: Mice in the US group were shaved, and the ultrasonic probe coated with ultrasonic coupling agent was targeted at the hippocampus (1.8 mm posterior, 1 mm lateral to Bregma) for 30 min per day (15 min on the left and 15 min on the right side) for 5 days.

flags.reason: Paper gives duty cycle (10%) and PRF (40 Hz) but never states pulse duration directly; not computed per instructions.
Only the ultrasound-exposed (US) group is counted; NC and AD sham groups (n=11 each) received no active ultrasound.
Paper does not state whether the 294 mW/cm2 Ispta value is a free-field or in-situ measurement.
Paper notes mice that died mid-experiment from surgical complications were excluded, but does not explicitly assess ultrasound-related adverse events.
